clue.text: My love put worm in drink as oxygenator

parts.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the worm is put inside the drink, so in signals one piece going into another

parts.note: gin is a spirit drink
a lob or lobworm is a lugworm used as bait

explanation.surface: A sweetheart drops a worm into a cocktail and calls it an oxygenator.
explanation.walkthrough: A lob, or lobworm, is the lugworm anglers use as bait; 'put' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Myoglobin is the muscle protein that stores and supplies oxygen, so it acts as an oxygen carrier.

clue.text: A bird takes in complaint of 8

taken as written
a tern is a seabird

explanation.definitionFit: Maternal is the adjective for things belonging to or like a mother.

clue.text: Report of dislike for old theatre

parts.note: odium is hatred or strong dislike

explanation.surface: Word gets round about an aversion to an ancient playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeum was a roofed building in ancient Greece or Rome for musical and dramatic performance.

clue.text: Slippers tied to rock by 8s?

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters of the preceding words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Slippers are lashed to a rock by a group of mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is MOTHER; read as people who go mothing, mothers are moth collectors, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepidopterists study butterflies and moths, so a moth hunter is one; the question mark flags the punning sense.

clue.text: See 8
Gaslight swallowed little baby

explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn child, especially in its first four weeks.

clue.text: Check front of boat

definitions.meaning: to ... a flow is to stop or check it
the upright timber at the bow of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Stem means both to halt something and the foremost part of a vessel's hull.

clue.text: Article on little bird said to have writers

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: said tells us the word for a young bird is spoken, not written

parts.note: a cygnet is a young swan

explanation.surface: A piece about a fledgling is reported to have attracted authors.
explanation.walkthrough: Writers to the Signet are a society of Scottish solicitors, so the Signet is what has its writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish solicitors belong to the Society of Writers to His Majesty's Signet, so that seal has writers attached.

clue.text: Test hero to go down with club lest beaten in fight with Saddam

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles
taken as written
to fall is to go down
a bat is a club for hitting a ball

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are beaten, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Test cricket hero falls, armed with a bat, lest he be beaten in a war against Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: Saddam Hussein promised the 'mother of all battles' in the 1991 Gulf War. 'beaten' rearranges LEST to TLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddam Hussein used this phrase for the coming Gulf War, and it became an idiom for a huge contest.

clue.text: Backing gamble from the heart, perhaps, to keep local from one part of skeleton

indicators.note: the pub and the one hold the turned-round piece between them, keeping one from the other

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub or inn
taken as written

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the gamble and the Latin phrase are read in reverse

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
Latin animo, as in ex animo, means from the heart or mind; perhaps marks the loose rendering

explanation.surface: A heartfelt bet made to keep a pub away from someone, written in anatomy-speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns the gamble and the Latin together into OMINATEB, which 'to keep' sets between the pub and the one; 'from' is a link. 'Perhaps' admits ANIMO is Latin, as in ex animo.
explanation.definitionFit: The innominate bone is the hip bone, formed from the fused ilium, ischium and pubis.

clue.text: Pipsqueak dropping article somewhere in Belgium

parts.note: Antwerp is a Belgian port city

explanation.surface: A little nobody sheds a word on the way through a Belgian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal names for a silly, insignificant person.

clue.text: God brandishing net is most problematic

explanation.walkthrough: 'brandishing' gives NIEST, the jumbled letters of the two words after the god.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorny means full of difficulties, so the superlative means the hardest to deal with.

clue.text: Make spray of potato, miserably late

explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the end of 'potato' and runs into 'miserably'; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To atomise a liquid is to reduce it to a fine mist of droplets.

clue.text: Changing the subject, an expert's a great lake among poor ponds

parts.note: a form of the indefinite article

indicators.note: the lake goes among the jumbled ponds, so among signals insertion
poor here means badly made, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: An expert shows a great lake set amid shabby ponds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' jumbles the five letters into POSDN; the lake then sits before its final N.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means apropos of nothing, used when changing topic without any link.

clue.text: Dress for 8's part in a tedious performance
